A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, added, and removed material to be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 4 and G report original attack experiments on the 885-sample pool, covering 15 victim models across the main text and appendix, with ablations and post-success analyses.

after.justification: Sections 4 and B report original results for 19 victim models, additional editor experiments, and comparisons with newly evaluated attack baselines.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.1–3.2 remove explicit history maintenance, MetaDiagnose, and SelectStrategy from the stated procedure, retaining the A–F strategy library as prompt guidance. The scoring rule replaces weighted L2/L1/nonempty priorities with binary valid-L1 success and replaces sweet-spot-weighted cosine quality with average cosine similarity. These substantially revise the reported refinement procedure, although retrieval and cumulative overlays remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 885-sample grounding pool drawn from OS-Atlas, SeeClick, AMEX, and ShowUI across mobile, desktop, and web environments, with the same icon-source corpora. Added victim models and controls do not introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained Random Injection baseline, v2 evaluates GPTFuzz-UI, LLM-Bank-Square-UI, and Random-BBox in Table 5. These introduce substantive corpus-mutation, descriptor-bank spatial-search, and randomized-placement comparators absent from v1.

E3.justification: V2 adds GUI-Owl-1.5 at 2B/4B/8B/32B, controlled editor swaps, and comparisons matching the D=5, pass@3 victim-query budget, max_edits=3, icon pool, Overlapper, and filters. Editor-call budgets differ explicitly between baselines. The original sample pool, L1/L2 criteria, and depth/icon-budget evaluation axes are retained.

E4.justification: V1's history/strategy ablation in Appendix G.2, Table 7 is removed. V2 adds editor-model ablations in Table 4 and the Random-BBox placement control in Table 5, substantially changing the mechanisms investigated. The parallel-width ablation and qualitative examples remain, while the post-success analysis is revised.

E5.justification: V2 Section 4.3 newly reports statistical significance using a McNemar test for the adapted-baseline comparisons. V1 reports no significance tests. V2 supplies no corresponding p-values or test statistics and adds no repeated-run, seed, or confidence-interval reporting.

E6.justification: Depth-table values for all 15 shared victims are unchanged, but v2 adds four GUI-Owl-1.5 configurations and editor/baseline results, and removes the history/strategy ablation results. Table 3 substantially revises post-success L1/L2: GO-opt. on UI-TARS changes from 89.95/2.77% to 47.84/20.00%, and UT-opt. on GUI-Owl from 81.75/2.04% to 45.20/15.48%. The PDFs do not explain these numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The formal score definition changes from v1 Equations 2–3 to v2 Equation 2, removing the gamma-weighted success accumulator and its ordering assumption. This is a substantive but localized mathematical-definition change. The non-triviality inequalities remain unchanged; neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction drops history-driven target adaptation as a core contribution and adds claims of editor independence and superiority over stronger adapted baselines. Headline evaluation scope expands to 19 models, although v1 already reports 15 including its appendix. The infrastructure contribution changes from developing a framework to publicly releasing it.

C2.justification: V1 interprets cross-optimized attacks as broadly disorienting but weak at attracting clicks to the injected icon; v2 instead concludes that icon-level confusion transfers strongly with only marginal target specificity. V2 also adds interpretations concerning editor-family alignment and the relative contributions of descriptions and placement, while removing the explanation that accumulated history is the dominant refinement mechanism.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a public code URL, detailed baseline construction and LLM-call budgets in Appendix B.3, and GUI-Owl-1.5 preprocessing and coordinate settings in B.4. Conversely, the detailed editor system and user prompts in v1 Appendix H.2 are explicitly omitted from v2 C.2. These materially change the available replication information.

R1.justification: V2 adds connections to Square Attack, Sparse-RS, and GPTFuzzer/LLM-Fuzzer through the adapted baselines, alongside GUI-Owl-1.5, editor-model, and additional safety/reasoning references. Most related-work discussion and the central novelty positioning remain stable; publication-metadata updates do not represent new works.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting affects the introduction, conclusion, Section 3.2, and post-success discussion. The extensive editor-prompt appendix becomes a short summary, and the experimental narrative gains Section 4.3 and a baseline-implementation subsection. Author ordering, affiliations, contribution notes, and acknowledgements also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redesigned with a construction pipeline and reorganized pool displays; Figures 3–4 gain curves and revised legends. Table 1 expands and groups victim rows, Table 3 is reorganized by victim, two new comparison tables appear, and the history/strategy table disappears. Figures 5–10 retain the same qualitative images.

improvement.justification: The editor ablations and matched-baseline comparisons materially strengthen empirical support. However, v2 changes the stated algorithm while retaining earlier depth results, substantially revises Table 3 without explanation, and omits detailed editor prompts. Its abstract still describes failure-based prompt adaptation absent from Algorithm 1. These gains coexist with unresolved method/result consistency and reproducibility tradeoffs, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
